title: 16 Aug 2026 (Taif)
des: Saudi Prometric paediatrics recall, Taif, 16 August 2026

questions.question: What is the main job of the leader of a CPR team?
questions.exp: The leader stands back, assigns roles and uses closed-loop communication.
questions.a: Ensure clear communication between team members

questions.question: A child needs a lumbar puncture but the parents refuse. What do you do?
questions.exp: Without consent (and outside an emergency where delay risks life), a procedure is not done; keep treating empirically.
questions.b: Do not do it; explain the risks and document the refusal

questions.question: A 14-year-old needs an appendicectomy. The parents agree but the child is afraid because a friend died during surgery. What do you do?
questions.exp: Seek the adolescent's assent by addressing his fears; parental consent is legally valid.
questions.b: Try to convince the child first, then operate

questions.question: A hospital with a good reputation runs research on a new drug. What makes the research ethical?
questions.exp: Ethics committee approval and informed consent with full disclosure.

questions.question: A doctor working at a government hospital and a private clinic refers patients to his clinic. What is this?
questions.exp: Using a public post to benefit private practice is a conflict of interest.

questions.question: A boy says his mother loves his sister more and fights with his sister. What do you advise?
questions.exp: Sibling rivalry needs parental behaviour management.

questions.question: While breaking bad news, the mother leaves and refuses to listen. What do you do?
questions.exp: Respect her wish; inform the other parent.
questions.b: Continue with the father in the mother's absence

questions.question: A lab result is given by phone. What do you do?
questions.exp: Write down and read back critical results.
questions.d: Listen, write it down and read it back

questions.question: A child argues with adults and blames others for his mistakes. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: ODD: angry, argumentative, defiant behaviour towards authority without serious rule violations.

questions.question: A child has a skull fracture, multiple bruises and cigarette burns from his father. What do you do?
questions.exp: Suspected abuse must be reported and the child kept safe.
questions.b: Report child abuse to the authorities

questions.question: Which describes judging an action as right or wrong by its outcome or consequences?
questions.exp: The recall gave this definition under "procedural justice", but judging by outcome is consequentialism; procedural justice is about fair process.

questions.question: An 18-month-old screams, kicks and bites during tantrums. What do you advise?
questions.exp: Time out of about 1 minute per year of age.

questions.question: A prescription has an error: "sub cut" was written. What is the correct practice?
questions.exp: Abbreviations like SC/SQ are error-prone; write in full.

questions.question: A doctor rudely interrupts a nurse. What principle does this breach?
questions.exp: Disrespectful treatment of staff breaches procedural justice.

questions.question: A sick child given vancomycin develops a rash. What do you do?
questions.exp: Adverse drug reactions are documented and reported to the regulator.
questions.c: Document it in the file and report it to the Saudi FDA

questions.question: A child cries when left with the babysitter and at school. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Distress on separation from attachment figures beyond the expected age is separation anxiety.

questions.question: A doctor neglects his patients and you suspect he may be addicted. What do you do?
questions.exp: Speak to the colleague first and escalate to the supervisor if patients are at risk.
questions.b: Talk to him and advise him to seek help

questions.question: An asthmatic child was caught in a house fire. What is the best first investigation?
questions.exp: Oximetry reads COHb as oxyhaemoglobin; measure COHb.

questions.question: A child swallowed a coin and can drink water. What is the best management?
questions.exp: A coin that has passed (child drinks) can be retrieved under fluoroscopy; the recall writer chose urgent oesophagoscopy, which is for symptomatic impacted coins and button batteries.
questions.d: Fluoroscopy-guided removal with a magnet or stylet

questions.question: After acute otitis media there is a middle ear effusion. What do you do?
A child looks ill with a rash and headache, GCS 10 and high WBC. What do you do first?
questions.exp: With reduced consciousness (GCS ≤ 12) LP is contraindicated; take blood cultures and start antibiotics.

questions.question: A child has a barking cough and stridor (laryngotracheobronchitis). What is the diagnosis?
An 18-month-old chokes suddenly and comes to the ER. What is the most common site of the foreign body?
A child is drooling and toxic in the ER. What is the best next step?
questions.exp: Suspected epiglottitis needs the airway secured by experts.

questions.question: Cystic fibrosis is commonly associated with which acid-base abnormality?
A child took a tricyclic antidepressant and the ECG shows VT. Besides sodium bicarbonate, which antiarrhythmic is recommended?
questions.exp: Class Ia drugs (procainamide, quinidine) worsen TCA toxicity; bicarbonate first, then lidocaine.

questions.question: How is fragile X syndrome diagnosed?
How is Werdnig-Hoffmann disease (SMA type 1) diagnosed?
How is Turner syndrome diagnosed?
A child with asthma has daily symptoms and FEV1 70%. What is the classification?
questions.exp: Daily symptoms with FEV1 60-80% is moderate persistent.

questions.question: A child has a facial port-wine stain and seizures (Sturge-Weber). What should you look for?
A child with pneumonia on ceftriaxone for 3 days is still distressed with an effusion. What do you do?
questions.exp: Drain a large or infected effusion.

questions.question: How fast does length increase in the second 3 months of life?
A child got angry, cried, then turned blue and lost consciousness and convulsed for 45 seconds. What do you do?
questions.exp: Cyanotic breath-holding spells can end in a brief anoxic seizure and are benign.

questions.question: A child has hyperreflexia, sudden decreased lower limb power and a positive Babinski sign. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Upper motor neuron signs with a sensory level.

questions.question: A child cannot stand suddenly after an URTI. He is normal except for ataxia and CT is normal. What is the diagnosis?
A 4-month-old's head circumference went from 35 to 47 cm with no change in suckling. What do you do?
questions.exp: Ultrasound through the fontanelle is first for a well infant with fast head growth.

questions.question: A child has repeated bitemporal headaches and abdominal pain. What is the diagnosis?
What is the acute treatment of migraine in an adolescent if ibuprofen fails?
What most likely causes a decrease in red cell 2,3-DPG?
questions.exp: Acidosis reduces 2,3-DPG; hypoxia, anaemia and altitude raise it.

questions.question: How is parotitis (mumps) diagnosed?
questions.exp: Virus from saliva (buccal swab) confirms mumps.
questions.d: Culture or PCR of parotid secretions

questions.question: Which pneumonia needs follow-up X-ray?
questions.exp: Round pneumonia may hide a mass.

questions.question: A child is well after trauma, then one hour later has a low GCS. What is the diagnosis?
What is a common complication of tetralogy of Fallot?
Oligaemic lung fields with a boot-shaped heart suggest which lesion?
After TOF surgery a child develops VF on the ECG. What is the treatment?
A child of height 115 cm has a systolic murmur and thrill at the right sternal border. What is the lesion?
A 9-month-old with a 9 mm VSD weighs only 5 kg on furosemide, spironolactone, captopril and digoxin. What is next?
questions.exp: Failure to thrive on maximal therapy needs repair.

questions.question: A child has lower limb weakness and a sensory level. What will MRI show?
questions.exp: Enhancing cord lesion in transverse myelitis.

questions.question: An ECG shows peaked T waves (hyperkalaemia). What do you give?
A boy's mother is 155 cm and father is 178 cm. What is his expected adult height?
After gastroenteritis a child develops ataxia and loss of bladder control. What is the investigation?
An infant has extension spasms of the limbs and trunk with irregular spike-and-wave EEG. What is the diagnosis?
A picture shows erythema toxicum in a newborn. What is found in the pustules?
A child with scleroderma (anti-Scl-70, anti-centromere) has a complication. What is it?
A child has recurrent typical febrile seizures and the mother is worried. What do you do?
A 9-month-old with gastroenteritis has head lag. What do you do?
questions.exp: Hypotonia may be from illness and dehydration; reassess when rehydrated.

questions.question: After a pull-through for Hirschsprung disease, the child has enterocolitis. What is the treatment?
A picture shows a child with features of hypothyroidism. What is the diagnosis?
A child with CF has an infection resistant to antibiotics. What is the organism?
Cryoprecipitate contains which factor?
An asthmatic child was admitted to PICU. What do you give at discharge?
questions.exp: A severe attack means controller therapy.

questions.question: What is seen in urine in glomerulonephritis?
A child has failure to thrive, metabolic alkalosis and diarrhoea. What urine test helps?
questions.exp: Low urine chloride means GI loss (e.g., congenital chloride diarrhoea); high means renal loss (Bartter).

questions.question: A girl cannot comb her hair and has proximal weakness. What is the test?
A child has a febrile seizure for 3 minutes with a 30-minute post-ictal phase. What is the management?
questions.exp: Short generalised febrile seizure: reassurance. Some recalls key EEG if the post-ictal phase is prolonged.

questions.question: Which is a vitamin K-dependent factor?
An infant has nasal congestion and obstruction but is well and feeding. What do you do?
A picture shows a child with mastoiditis. What do you do?
questions.exp: Mastoiditis needs IV antibiotics, ENT review and imaging.
questions.b: Admit for IV antibiotics and CT if complications

questions.question: A 6-year-old has dullness and bronchial breathing on the right with crackles on the left (X-ray). What is the treatment?
questions.exp: The recall keyed azithromycin for school-age (atypical) pneumonia.

questions.question: An asthmatic child in the ER has wheeze and reduced air entry. What do you give?
A neutropenic child on chemotherapy has fever with no focus. Which organism must empirical antibiotics always cover?
questions.exp: Febrile neutropenia is treated at once with an antipseudomonal beta-lactam (piperacillin-tazobactam or cefepime), because Gram-negative sepsis can kill within hours.

questions.question: A 2-month-old fell from the bed and has impaired consciousness and bruises all over the body. What is the diagnosis?
A 32-week preterm baby on formula develops abdominal distension and green-yellow NG aspirates (picture). What is the diagnosis?
A newborn's Apgar score is calculated from a scenario. What was the recalled score?
questions.exp: The scenario gave a score of 4 (moderately depressed).

questions.question: An 18-month-old girl took a deep breath during a fight over a toy, stopped breathing and had tonic movements for seconds. She is normal now. What do you do?
A boy had eye blinking, then throat clearing, and over years another tic. How is the diagnosis made?
A CT picture shows a brain abscess. What is the treatment?
A child is treated for iron deficiency anaemia. Which parameter increases first?
A haemophilia patient does not improve after factor VIII. What is next?
A patient has potassium 8.5. What is the next step?
questions.exp: ECG and cardiac monitoring, with calcium if changes.

questions.question: A 5-year-old has painless maroon rectal bleeding; examination and tests are otherwise normal. What is next?
What is the best way to assess pain in an infant?
An 8-month-old has diarrhoea after jarred food and juice. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Symptoms start with fructose-containing fruit and juice.

questions.question: A child recognises 3 colours, knows his full name and age, rides a tricycle but cannot copy a square. What is the developmental age?
questions.exp: Tricycle and circle at 3; square at 4.

questions.question: A child has recurrent infections and pneumonia, low IgA and IgG, a positive Romberg sign and deterioration. What is the diagnosis?
A child with ataxia has recurrent pneumonias with low IgA and IgG. Which test helps the diagnosis?
A child with coeliac disease has itchy vesicles on extensor surfaces (picture). What is the diagnosis?
A child with otitis media on day 3 of treatment becomes irritable. What do you do?
A child has a high-pitched voice in a long scenario of growth failure. What is the hormonal defect?
questions.exp: GH deficiency gives a high-pitched voice and doll face.

questions.question: A short child with a high-pitched voice has growth hormone deficiency. What is the treatment?
A child has a simple febrile convulsion. What do you do?
A child with vomiting and nausea took a TCA overdose. What is the antidote for cardiotoxicity?
A picture shows a neonate with a fungal rash in the neck folds. What is the treatment?
A child has ADHD. What is the drug of choice?
A 3-year-old was normal until 2 years, then stopped responding, looks at the sky and has repetitive movements. What is the diagnosis?
An infant has no head lag and looks at his hands. What is the age?
questions.exp: Head control and hand regard at about 3-4 months.

questions.question: A child has a vesicular rash on the skin and in the mouth. What is the treatment?
questions.exp: The recall keyed acyclovir; it helps herpetic gingivostomatitis or varicella if started early.

questions.question: A child with diabetes has recurrent hypoglycaemia. Which test assesses long-term glycaemic control?
What is a poor prognostic sign in TCA poisoning?
questions.exp: Hypotension, QRS > 100 ms and seizures predict poor outcome.

questions.question: A child has failure to thrive, Na 170 and high BP. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Severe hypernatraemia with hypertension and no dehydration suggests salt poisoning.

questions.question: A neonate has a mass coming from the nose. What is the next step?
A picture shows an NG tube that will not pass beyond the stomach. What is the diagnosis?
A child has a foreign body obstructing the pylorus and an NG tube cannot pass. What is the management?
How does indomethacin for PDA compare in preterm and term infants?
questions.exp: The term ductus responds poorly to prostaglandin inhibitors.
questions.c: Better in preterm than full-term infants

questions.question: A 2-day-old has not passed meconium, has distension and bilious vomiting, and a gush of meconium after PR with an empty rectum. What is the diagnosis?
A child has bone pain, high phosphate, high calcium, high ALP, high PTH and abnormal renal function. What is the diagnosis?
A child has bone pain with high phosphate, ALP and PTH and abnormal renal function. What is the next investigation?
A child has normal calcium, high ALP, high PTH, low phosphate and high urinary phosphate. What is the diagnosis?
A 7-month-old girl suddenly extends both legs and grunts, then stops. She is normal and EEG is normal. What do you do?
A child has culture-confirmed streptococcal pharyngitis treated with penicillin. For how long?
A picture shows a malar rash (SLE). Which test is most specific?
A neonate on day 1 has pustules (transient neonatal pustular melanosis). What do you do?
A picture shows a newborn with a midline skull defect containing brain. What is the diagnosis?
A child has worsening school performance and tremor. What is the investigation?
questions.exp: The recall keyed liver biopsy; ceruloplasmin and 24-h urine copper come first, liver copper confirms.
questions.c: Serum ceruloplasmin (and liver biopsy for copper)

questions.question: A 3-month-old has cough and fever 39 with family members who have URTI. What is the diagnosis?
A child has urinary and stool incontinence. What is the investigation?
questions.exp: Tethered cord or occult spinal dysraphism.

questions.question: For how long is CPR usually continued before stopping if there is no response?
questions.exp: Recalls key 20 minutes, decided by the team leader.

questions.question: What should you wear first when caring for a child with pneumonia under droplet/contact precautions?
questions.exp: Donning order: gown, mask, goggles, gloves.

questions.question: Which condition needs a special environment for examination?
A boy has soiling since toilet training, impacted stool and decreased anal tone. What is the investigation?
questions.exp: Low anal tone suggests a spinal cause.

questions.question: A child with rheumatic heart disease who injects drugs has fever, hepatosplenomegaly and a new murmur. What is the diagnosis?
A 6-month-old cries and has gum swelling. What do you advise?
questions.exp: Benzocaine gels are not advised in infants.
questions.c: Cold teething ring and simple analgesia

questions.question: A child has asthma that worsens in winter. What do you advise?
What is a feature of third cranial nerve palsy?
questions.exp: Ptosis, dilated pupil, eye down and out.

questions.question: A picture shows a scrotal swelling with positive transillumination. What is the diagnosis?
A child ingested his mother's iron tablets and is unwell. What is the treatment?
A child has small platelets and thrombocytopenia. What is the diagnosis?
A 4-month-old's HC was 32 cm at birth and is now 36 cm. What is the investigation?
A medication error occurred between two drugs with similar names. What is this called?
A child with ALL had abdominal pain, surgery and bloody diarrhoea, with necrotic bowel on the picture. What is the diagnosis?
What is an indication for splenectomy in sickle cell disease?
A child on prednisolone 25 mg/day develops severe abdominal pain with guarding and marked tenderness. What is the management?
questions.exp: Steroids mask perforation; peritonism needs surgery. The recall writer chose ceftriaxone.

questions.question: A child has a puffy face, low activity and skin crusting on the shins. What is the diagnosis?
A newborn cyanosed on day 1 improved after atrial septostomy. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Balloon septostomy improves mixing in TGA.

questions.question: A 3-year-old has cough, dyspnoea, fever 39 and rhonchi. What is the diagnosis?
What is part of the secondary survey in trauma?
A child wakes screaming 1-2 hours after sleep and has no memory next morning. What is it?
An infant has bouts of coughing that end in cyanosis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Paroxysmal cough ending in cyanosis, a whoop or vomiting is pertussis. The recall writer chose bronchitis.

questions.question: A 5-year-old has pneumonia with Gram-positive cocci. What is the treatment?
What arrhythmia is found after surgical correction of TGA?
questions.exp: Sinus node dysfunction after atrial switch.

questions.question: A 2-year-old has dark urine, abdominal pain, tenderness, BP 110/80, fever 39.8, protein ++, RBC >10 and WBC >10. What is the investigation?
A child has raised intracranial pressure with severe headache. What sign is most important to look for?
questions.exp: Focal signs suggest a mass lesion.

questions.question: A child has a foul-smelling nasal discharge from a foreign body. What do you do?
questions.exp: Recalls key admission and ENT referral.
questions.d: Admit and refer to ENT for removal

questions.question: A 3-month-old has poor feeding, sweating with feeds, tachypnoea, poor weight gain, heart failure and a loud pansystolic murmur with a thrill at the LLSB. What is the diagnosis?
A baby collapses in the ER; the ECG shows electrical activity but no carotid pulse. What is the diagnosis?
Which cardiac lesion most commonly leads to pulmonary hypertension?
What is the treatment of chronic hepatitis C in an adolescent?
questions.exp: Direct-acting antivirals (glecaprevir-pibrentasvir) are approved from 3 years. The recall's option names were garbled.

questions.question: An infant has recurrent epistaxis and uses local nasal steroids. What is the most likely cause?
questions.exp: Allergic rhinitis and steroid sprays dry the mucosa.

questions.question: A picture shows a sunburst bone lesion. What is it?
Meconium ileus is associated with which disease?
A 10-year-old has jaundice, ascites, prolonged PT/INR, high ALT/AST, high ammonia and confusion. What is the diagnosis?
How often are the lungs involved in SLE?
questions.exp: Pleuritis and lung disease in about half.

questions.question: A drowned child has hyperglycaemia (18 mmol/L). What do you give?
MRSA is in the hospital. What precautions?
How does MRSA spread in a hospital?
What is the most common abdominal tumour in toddlers?
questions.exp: Wilms in the recall; neuroblastoma is commoner in infancy.

questions.question: A child has high TSH, low T4, short stature, eyelid oedema and calf muscle hypertrophy. What is the syndrome?
A child has a rectal polyp, bloody stool and a family history of colorectal cancer. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Multiple juvenile polyps with family history.

questions.question: A patient discharged after acute pancreatitis returns 10 days later with epigastric pain and tenderness. What do you do?
questions.exp: Look for a pseudocyst (CT or US).

questions.question: A child has painless rectal bleeding. What is the most likely cause?
A 6-year-old girl develops new nocturnal enuresis with lower abdominal pain. Urine has WBC >10, RBC >10, protein 2+, BP 110/73 and anaemia. What is the diagnosis?
A 6-year-old has acute pyelonephritis and needs IV treatment. What is the treatment?
A child has a nasal polyp. What is the investigation?
A 12-year-old after URTI has jaundice, high bilirubin, joint pain and high ALP. What is the diagnosis?
A newborn has respiratory distress and a cystic chest lesion since birth. What is the investigation?
A child has signs of shock with cold extremities and hypotension. What finding do you expect?
A 7-year-old's sibling with ALL had a BMT 18 months ago and now has chickenpox today. What do you give the transplant patient?
A 10-year-old who was toilet trained at 4 now has urinary and faecal incontinence. What is the investigation?
When is ileoileal intussusception more common?
A child has lockjaw after a wound. What is the diagnosis?
A child has muffled heart sounds, distended neck veins, hypotension and cold extremities. What is the diagnosis?
A patient has three episodes of confusion over a week with focal seizures. What is the investigation?
A child copied Superman from TV, fell and fractured his arm. What is the advice?
questions.d: Control and supervise what the child watches

questions.question: A 10-year-old has bloody diarrhoea, failure to thrive (height and weight below the 3rd centile), recurrent abdominal pain and anaemia. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Growth failure is typical of Crohn.

questions.question: Which test confirms beta thalassaemia major?
questions.exp: HbF high with absent or low HbA on HPLC confirms thalassaemia major. The recall writer chose bone marrow aspiration.

questions.question: A child with dengue has headache, fever and epigastric pain but no warning signs. What do you do?
questions.exp: Dengue without warning signs is managed at home with fluids; avoid NSAIDs and aspirin.
questions.b: Discharge with oral fluids (ORS) and paracetamol
